summary: Temporary support with basic living needs during financial difficulty.
eligibility_text: Temporary support for families and individuals who are unable to work for a period of time (e.g. due to illness, caregiving responsibilities), are looking for a job, or are earning a low income and require assistance to meet their basic living needs.
benefit_text: ComCare provides financial assistance and social support to individuals and families who need help with their daily living expenses.
source_title: Ministry of Social and Family Development

summary: Long-term support where a person cannot work and has little income or family support.
eligibility_text: Long-term support for persons who are permanently unable to work due to old age, illness or disability, have limited or no means of income, and have little or no family support.
benefit_text: ComCare provides financial assistance and social support to individuals and families who need help with their daily living expenses.
source_title: Ministry of Social and Family Development

summary: Healthcare subsidies, with benefit tiers based on household income or home annual value.
eligibility_text: All Singapore Citizens are eligible for CHAS. The CHAS benefits will be tiered according to household monthly income per person or the Annual Value (AV) of the home, as indicated in the table below: CHAS Criteria CHAS Green CHAS Orange CHAS Blue ^Household monthly income per person (for households with income) Above $2,300 $1,501 - $2,300 $1,500 and below ^^Annual Value (AV) of home (for households with no income) Above $31,000 $21,001 - $31,000 $21,000 and below ^ Household monthly income per person is the total gross household monthly income divided by total number of family members living together. Gross monthly income refers to your basic employment income, trade/self-employed income, overtime pay, allowances, cash awards, commissions, and bonuses. ^^ Annual Value is the estimated gross annual rent of a property if it were to be rented out, excluding furnishings and maintenance fees. It is determined by IRAS and may be checked via mytax.iras.gov.sg . While every Singapore Citizen is eligible for CHAS, the enrolment onto CHAS is still on an application basis. To enjoy subsidies under CHAS, households are required to submit an application. Singapore Citizens who have the Public Assistance (PA) card do not need to apply for CHAS, as they can already receive full CHAS subsidies by showing the PA card.
benefit_text: While every Singapore Citizen is eligible for CHAS, the enrolment onto CHAS is still on an application basis. To enjoy subsidies under CHAS, households are required to submit an application.
source_title: Eligibility

summary: Credit for approved skills development and lifelong learning courses.
eligibility_text: All Singapore Citizens aged 25 and above
benefit_text: Types of SkillsFuture Credit 1. Opening SkillsFuture Credit — $500 This base tier credit can be used on top of existing SkillsFuture course fee subsidies to pay for a wide range of approved skills-related courses. It has no expiry date and is provided to all Singapore Citizens aged 25 and above. All courses listed on MySkillsFuture portal are eligible for SkillsFuture Credit (Opening Credit). They include: Courses subsidised or approved by the Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA), Selected courses offered by Ministry of Education-funded institutions such as Institute of Technical Education, polytechnics, autonomous universities, LASALLE College of the Arts and Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts, Courses supported by lead agencies, and SkillsFuture@PA courses offered by the People’s Association and selected courses under the National Silver Academy. 2. SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) — $4,000 This credit supports Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above. It can be used to offset out-of-pocket course fees for selected courses that have better employability outcomes, and it does not expire. Eligible courses include: Institute of Higher Learning (IHL) full qualifications and shorter modules that stack to a full qualification, MOE-subsidised full qualifications from the University of the Arts Singapore and Arts Institutions, SkillsFuture Career Transition Programmes (SCTP), which are train-and-place programmes in sectors with good hiring opportunities, Courses aligned to training requirements in Progressive Wage Model (PWM) sectors, and Workplace Literacy and Numeracy courses. Note : Any balance from the one-off Additional SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career Support) , which was provided to every Singapore Citizen aged 40 to 60 (inclusive) as at 31 December 2020, is now merged with the SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) and no longer carries an expiry date. source_title: SkillsFuture Credit | Education, Career and Personal Development

summary: Means-tested kindergarten fee support, including special approval for some ComCare and public rental households.
eligibility_text: All Singapore Citizen (SC) children enrolled at an Anchor Operator (AOP) or Ministry of Education (MOE) kindergarten are eligible for means-tested subsidies under the KiFAS if their monthly gross household income is $12,000 or less, or per capita income is $3,000 or less (for households with 5 or more members). Find out how HHI and PCI are assessed Non-Parent Caregivers If you are a non-parent caregiver (i.e. legal guardian, guardian, head of children’s home) caring for a SC child enrolled at an AOP or MOE kindergarten, you can apply to receive KiFAS subsidy on a time-limited basis. Note: Foster parents who are already receiving a fostering allowance from the Ministry of Social and Family Development are not eligible for KiFAS subsidies. Households under the HDB’s Public Rental Scheme or MSF’s ComCare Assistance Families who are tenants of a rental flat under the HDB’s Public Rental Scheme or are beneficiaries of ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term or Long-Term Assistance will be eligible for maximum KiFAS subsidies under Special Approval until the next fixed point of subsidy assessment. Note: The approved KiFAS subsidies are valid until the next fixed point of subsidy assessment or until your child withdraws from the kindergarten, whichever comes first. Learn more about the fixed points of subsidy assessment. Your child must attend kindergarten for at least one day in the month to be eligible for the KiFAS subsidies for that month. The KiFAS subsidies will be paid directly to the kindergarten, and you are only required to pay the programme fees nett of subsidies.
benefit_text: The KiFAS subsidies will be paid directly to the kindergarten, and you are only required to pay the programme fees nett of subsidies.
source_title: ECDA | Overview of the Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme (KiFAS)

summary: Basic and means-tested additional subsidies for eligible preschool enrolments.
eligibility_text: Types of subsidies There are two types of subsidies under the infant and childcare subsidy scheme: Basic Subsidy All Singapore Citizen (SC) children enrolled in an ECDA-licensed infant or childcare centre are eligible for a Basic Subsidy. Additional Subsidy Your child will be eligible for Additional Subsidy if: The main applicant (mother or single father) is working at the point of the subsidy application; and The family's gross monthly household income (HHI) is $12,000 or below; or The per capita income (PCI) is $3,000 or below for households consisting of 5 or more family members who are related by blood, marriage, and/or legal adoption, and who share the same registered residential address. Find out how HHI and PCI are assessed
benefit_text: The exact amount of preschool subsidies that your child may receive depends on the following: The working status of the main subsidy applicant at the point of the subsidy application or fixed point of subsidy assessment . A 'working main applicant' refers to the mother (or single father for divorced, separation or widowed cases) who works at least 56 hours per month. This includes full-time, part-time and freelance work arrangements. Your family's means-tested income at the point of the subsidy application or fixed point of subsidy reassessment. Your child’s preschool programme (infant care or childcare) and service type (full-day, half-day, or flexi-care), and programme fee . Note: Household or personal expenses are not considered in the subsidy assessment. Estimate your child's preschool subsidy Please visit Search for preschools | LifeSG – Services and log in with your Singpass to search for preschools with information on estimated fees after subsidies. You may also refer to the table below to find out the amount of preschool subsidy your child may be eligible for, based on your household income (HHI) or per capita income (PCI). Childcare and Infant Care subsidy tables The amount of subsidies reflected is an estimate. The actual subsidy amount will be determined based on verified details, such as screened income. Note: The approved preschool subsidies are valid until the next fixed point of subsidy assessment or until your child withdraws from the preschool, whichever comes first. Learn more about the fixed points of subsidy assessment . Your child must attend preschool for at least one day in a month to be eligible for subsidies for that month. The subsidies will be paid directly to the preschool, and you are only required to pay the infant or childcare fees nett of subsidies.
source_title: ECDA | Overview of the infant and childcare subsidy scheme

summary: Financial assistance for school fees and expenses; the applicable scheme depends on the school or institution.
eligibility_text: Eligible Singapore Citizens (SC) studying in the following schools or institutions can receive financial assistance from MOE on fees and other school expenses: Government and government-aided schools Government-funded special education schools Independent schools Specialised schools Some specialised independent schools: NUS High School of Mathematics and Science and the School of Science and Technology Government-funded post-secondary education institutions: Institute of Technical Education, polytechnics, autonomous universities and arts institutions and National Institute of Early Childhood Development (NIEC).
benefit_text: The financial scheme your child can apply for depends on the type of school or institution they are studying in.
source_title: Financial assistance | MOE

summary: Support for capability development, efficiency and overseas expansion, replacing EDG, MRA and PSG for new applications.
eligibility_text: For Singapore companies starting new projects to upgrade capabilities, improve efficiency and expand overseas
benefit_text: Receive up to 70% for SMEs and up to 50% for non-SMEs Support levels differ by activity. Refer to each activity for more details. Access up to S$100,000 in total grant support per year, across all activities Use the funding where it matters most. The total grant support cap is shared across all activities and refreshed on 1 April each year. Grant support is disbursed on a reimbursement basis Claims can be submitted once the activity is completed and full payment has been made.
source_title: EDGE Grant

summary: Co-funding for energy-efficient equipment. Sector coverage and application conditions vary by tier.
eligibility_text: Eligibility Applicants must meet all the following eligibility criteria at the point of application for the respective tiers of support: Tier Eligibility Base tier Business entity registered and operating in Singapore in the following sectors: Construction companies classified under SSIC 41 to 43 Data Centres and their users (equipment purchased must be hosted at a commercial data centre in Singapore) Food Services companies with valid Singapore Food Agency (SFA) licence and classified under SSIC 56 or 68104 Maritime companies 1 which include: Port companies classified under SSIC 23940, 24109, 49231, 50021, 50023, 52101, 52221, 52222, 52224, 52243, 52292 Manufacturing companies classified under SSIC 10 to 32 (including Food Manufacturing) Retail companies classified under SSIC 47 Minimum of 30% local shareholding* Group Annual Sales Turnover of no more than S$500 million Equipment purchased must be used in Singapore * For users of data centres, business entities need not have a minimum of 30% local shareholding criteria. Advanced tier (only available for selected sectors) Business entity registered and operating in Singapore in the following sectors: Construction companies classified under SSIC 41 to 43 Manufacturing companies classified under SSIC 10 to 32 (including Food Manufacturing) Minimum of 30% local shareholding Group Annual Sales Turnover of no more than S$500 million Equipment purchased must be used in Singapore 1 Applications for EEG (Base) for the Harbourcraft sector and EEG (Advanced) for the Port sector closed on 31 March 2026. Companies may not be eligible for the grant if they have commenced procurement of the equipment at the point of grant application. The application may be rejected if any of the following have taken place before the application date: Companies have made payment to a third-party, who is part of the application
benefit_text: The EEG will provide two tiers of support – a base tier to provide support for pre-approved EE equipment up to S$30,000; and an advanced tier to support companies for larger investments that drive greater energy efficiency. More details in the table below: Tier Support Cap Per Company Qualifying Equipment Support Rate Base tier Up to S$30,000 Pre-approved EE equipment Government will support up to 70% and up to 30% for SMEs and non-SMEs respectively until 31 March 2027. Advanced tier (only available for selected sectors) Up to S$350,000 across base and enhanced tiers EE equipment need not be pre-approved, but must demonstrate energy savings above 350t lifetime carbon abatement Lower of: Support levels under the base tier; or Grant quantum computed based on EE equipment’s expected lifetime energy savings
source_title: Energy Efficiency Grant

scheme_name: Enterprise Financing Scheme – SME Working Capital Loan
summary: Financing for operational cashflow; a loan subject to financial institution assessment and full repayment.
eligibility_text: Eligibility Business entity registered and operating in Singapore ACRA-registered Sole Proprietorships, Partnerships, Limited Liability Partnerships and Companies are eligible to apply Approvals of loans are subject to the participating Financial Institution’s assessment. Company has at least 30% local equity held directly or indirectly by Singaporean(s) and/or Singapore PR(s), determined by the ultimate individual ownership Company has a Group Annual Sales Turnover not exceeding S$500 million For “SME Working Capital”, an SME is defined as having a Group revenue of up to S$100 million or a maximum employment size of 200 employees
benefit_text: Loan details Maximum Loan Quantum S$500,000 / borrower Note: Borrowers are subject to an overall borrower group limit of S$5 million for EFS-WCL. In addition, there is an overall loan exposure limit of S$50 million per borrower group 1 across all facilities. Maximum Repayment Period 5 years EnterpriseSG Risk-share Risk share is at 50% Young enterprises² may receive a risk share of 70%. From 1 Sep 2026 to 31 Mar 2027: Risk share for all enterprises will be 70%. The borrower is responsible to repay 100% of the loan amount When defaults occur, the participating Financial Institutions (FIs) are obligated to follow their standard commercial recovery procedure, including the realisation of security, before they can make a claim against EnterpriseSG for the unrecovered amount in proportion to the risk-share
source_title: Enterprise Financing Scheme – SME Working Capital Loan

summary: Financing for qualifying green technology providers and adopters, subject to bank approval and repayment.
eligibility_text: Eligibility Business entity registered and operating in Singapore ACRA-registered Sole Proprietorships, Partnerships, Limited Liability Partnerships and Companies are eligible to apply Approvals of loans are subject to the participating FI's assessment Company has at least 30% local equity held directly or indirectly by Singaporean(s) and/or Singapore PR(s), determined by the ultimate individual ownership Company's Group Annual Sales Turnover should not exceed S$500 million Meets the criteria for EFS-Green’s Qualifying Green Sectors and Activities and Qualifying Borrower Types View Qualifying Green Sectors and Activities View Qualifying Borrower Types Note: As announced at Budget 2024, EFS-Green will be expanded to include green solution adopters from 1 April 2024.
benefit_text: EnterpriseSG will provide 70% risk-share to catalyse the lending from participating Financial Institutions (FIs)
source_title: Enterprise Financing Scheme – Green

summary: Capability building, digital projects and implementation support for social service agencies.
eligibility_text: Eligibility criteria Applicant shall be of the following: Has the primary function of providing a social service or directly supporting the provision of a social service in Singapore. Registered under the Business Names Registration Act 2014, Societies Act, incorporated under the Companies Act or established by or under any written law. Has at least two years of continuous operation. Staff of agency should not chair the Board and should not comprise more than one-third of the Board Has a valid Organisational Health Framework for Social Services (OHFSS) assessment ↗ (opens in new tab) . Complete organisational health diagnostics to receive funding for non pre-scoped solutions (Part A and B).
benefit_text: Grant quantum Funding is available to SSAs across 3 components, at up to 80% co-funding and up to 3-years. Funding under this scheme is assessed on the merits of proposals. Proposals will be assessed on factors such as the agency's alignment to social service delivery, the relevance of the capability being built, the agency's need for funding support, the cost-effectiveness of the proposed approach, and the expected benefit to the sector. Part A – Consultancy and Project implementation support Funding of up to $250,000, capped at $200,000 for headcount support. Example: Engage consultants to conduct compensation and benefits review or develop and implement volunteer management framework. Fund project headcount to lead transformation projects. Part B - Bespoke digitalisation projects Funding of up to $150,000. Examples: Custom web portals for service delivery, AI chatbots for automated responses, or therapeutic robotics solutions. Part C – Pre-scoped and green-laned solutions Funding of up to $150,000 in total. Up to $40,000 per solution or refer to specific Green Lane solutions' funding cap. Examples: HR management systems, account management systems, event booking platforms, CRM systems, or API integrations. Agencies may refer to the list of pre-scoped and green lane solutions , e.g. digital systems, cybersecurity data protection consultancy, for more information.
source_title: Transformation Sustainability Scheme | National Council of Social Service

summary: Diagnostic consultancy and capability roadmaps for eligible social service agencies.
eligibility_text: Eligibility criteria Applicant shall be of the following: Has the primary function of providing a social service or directly supporting the provision of a social service in Singapore. Registered under the Business Names Registration Act 2014, Societies Act, incorporated under the Companies Act or established by or under any written law. Has at least two years of continuous operation. Staff of agency should not chair the Board and should not comprise more than one-third of the Board Has a valid Organisational Health Framework for Social Service Assessment ↗ (opens in new tab) .
benefit_text: Grant quantum Agencies can be supported with co-funding from NCSS at up to 80%. Funding under this scheme is assessed based on agencies grant proposal. Proposals will be assessed on factors such as the agency's commitment from leadership and the Board to organisational health, recent efforts undertaken to improve organisational health, and the agency's readiness to translate diagnostic findings into concrete capability building plans.
source_title: Organisation Health Diagnostic Scheme | National Council of Social Service

summary: Professional training and development support for staff in eligible social service agencies.
eligibility_text: Eligibility criteria Please note the general eligibility requirements for all schemes: Applicant eligibility: Applicant must be a staff member of an NCSS sector member agency and/or MSF-funded agency. Course eligibility: The selected course must be social service related. It should be directly relevant to the job scope of the social service agency applicant. Funding restrictions: Funding will not be extended to courses that have already commenced.
benefit_text: The grant is dedicated to strengthening social service agencies by enhancing their manpower and professional capacity. By providing broad based support through scholarships, career conversion, higher education sponsorships and short-term courses, the grant equips social service professionals with the skills and knowledge necessary to meet the sector's evolving needs and nurtures excellence. Social Service Institute (SSI) offers a host of training grants to support social service professional to develop skills and professional needs. With various types of funding support available, you can enjoy subsidies of up to 90% 1 for your course fees for both short courses and academic programmes. SSAs can nominate their employees for the Leadership Development Programme (LDP), Professional Development and Management Programme (PDMP) and Sabbatical Leave Scheme (SLS). To find out more information on the available funding support, please visit Professional Development Programmes . 1 Terms and conditions apply .
source_title: Professional Capability Grant | National Council of Social Service

summary: Support for artistic presentation and participation, with revised coverage from April 2026.
eligibility_text: The grant is open to individuals, organisations and collectives and supports: Music Recording Projects Publishing Exhibition/Performance Festivals/Conferences Proposed projects can be conducted via physical and/or digital means.
benefit_text: The National Arts Council (NAC)’s Presentation and Participation (P&P) Grant aims to enable a wide range of arts practitioners and organisations to express and enrich our artistic diversity, as well as increase arts appreciation and participation in Singapore.
source_title: Overview of the Presentation and Participation Grant | National Arts Council

summary: Professional development and on-the-job training for Singapore’s arts and culture sector.
eligibility_text: The grant is open to individuals and organisations and supports the following training activities or programmes that span a duration of no more than 12 consecutive months: Professional training and skills development programmes On-the-job training activities
benefit_text: Our funding varies by project type and applicant, as shown in the table below: Coverage Type For Individuals For Non-Profit Organisations or Collectives For Profit Organisations Percentage of Actual Supportable Expenses Up to 70% [For SEPs only] Up to 90% Up to 70% Up to 50% Overall Cap per Financial Year $20,000 $75,000 $75,000 Note: More information and list of supportable costs can be found in the grant guidelines.
source_title: Overview of the Capability Development Grant | National Arts Council

summary: Multi-disciplinary, use-inspired research addressing important real-world problems relevant to Singapore.
benefit_text: The CRP funds use-inspired basic research projects selected through a merit review process based on scientific excellence. The theme of the proposed research project must be motivated by an important need or problem to be solved.
source_title: Competitive Research Programme | National Research Foundation, Singapore (NRF)

summary: Independent research opportunities in Singapore for outstanding early career scientists across science and technology.
eligibility_text: The Singapore NRF Fellowship provides opportunities for early career researchers to carry out independent research in Singapore, over a five-year period. It is open to all areas of science and technology and outstanding young scientists and researchers of all nationalities are welcome to apply.
benefit_text: Each Fellow is provided with a research grant to support projects that exhibit high likelihood of a research breakthrough. The research grant can be used to cover personnel, equipment and consumables costs.
source_title: NRF Fellowship | National Research Foundation, Singapore (NRF)

summary: Support for excellent principal investigators pursuing ground-breaking, high-risk research.
eligibility_text: It is designed to support a small number of excellent Principal Investigators who have a track record of research achievements that identify them as leaders in their respective field(s) of research.
benefit_text: The NRF Investigatorship provides opportunities for scientists and researchers to pursue ground-breaking, high-risk research.
source_title: NRF Investigatorship | National Research Foundation, Singapore (NRF)

scheme_name: Industry Alignment Fund – Industry Collaboration Projects
summary: Strategic public-sector R&D with industry partners and a route to commercialisation or deployment.
eligibility_text: Eligibility IAF-ICP is open to all Public Research Institutions in Singapore to apply. Companies are not eligible to apply directly and will not be considered as co-applicants. All applications must be submitted by the Public Research Institutions - applications submitted directly by individual researchers will not be accepted. To qualify for IAF-ICP funding, Performers must seek Industry Partners who are willing to commit R&D spending (cash and in-kind) to the research project (i.e., Total Research and Innovation Expenditure ( TRIE )).
benefit_text: The Industry Alignment Fund – Industry Collaboration Projects (IAF-ICP) is a pan-domain grant scheme that supports public research performers in strategic R&D projects with industry.
source_title: IAF-ICP
